 Sandia National Laboratories publishes study on deflecting irregular asteroids
 Jordan Honeycutt Updated 2026년 11월 4일 수 오전 3:58 UTC 0 ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. (KRQE) – Sandia National Laboratory is studying how nuclear X-ray blasts could help deflect an asteroid headed to Earth, nudging it off course and saving the planet. Researcher Nathan Moore said older simulations used a sphere to represent a possible asteroid, which made the math easier, but most asteroids are actually lumpy, irregular shapes.

 Now, scientists are using new simulations to figure out how to push an oddly-shaped object off course, without exploding it completely, as that could still send deadly pieces down to Earth. Sandia Labs published the findings in the scientific journal Icarus last month, reducing the guesswork needed to avoid doomsday.
